findings.title: If reading the keychain fails for any reason other than 'no entry', the code treats it as an empty vault and returns the config with blank secrets; the frontend then holds blank secrets and its next save writes them back, overwriting every stored secret with blanks.
findings.description: If reading the keychain fails for any reason other than 'no entry', the code treats it as an empty vault and returns the config with blank secrets; the frontend then holds blank secrets and its next save writes them back, overwriting every stored secret with blanks.

findings.title: The migration of old plaintext secrets into the keychain only triggers when the ElevenLabs key or the access token is set, so a config holding only the Drive client secret or refresh token is never migrated and keeps those secrets in config.json.
findings.description: The migration of old plaintext secrets into the keychain only triggers when the ElevenLabs key or the access token is set, so a config holding only the Drive client secret or refresh token is never migrated and keeps those secrets in config.json.

findings.title: After moving secrets to the keychain the code rewrites config.json to strip them but ignores a failed write, and it has no completion marker, so the plaintext secrets can stay on disk and the migration reruns on every config load.
findings.description: After moving secrets to the keychain the code rewrites config.json to strip them but ignores a failed write, and it has no completion marker, so the plaintext secrets can stay on disk and the migration reruns on every config load.

findings.title: The dev-mode sync of the config to static/_config.json returns early when the API key is empty, but it is always called with the already-sanitized config whose key is empty, so the sync never happens.
findings.description: The dev-mode sync of the config to static/_config.json returns early when the API key is empty, but it is always called with the already-sanitized config whose key is empty, so the sync never happens.

findings.quote: // Removed automatic public sharing — screen recordings may contain sensitive content.
findings.title: The change removes automatic public sharing of uploaded recordings from the Rust Drive upload, but the browser upload path in the preview page still makes every uploaded file readable by anyone with the link.
findings.description: The change removes automatic public sharing of uploaded recordings from the Rust Drive upload, but the browser upload path in the preview page still makes every uploaded file readable by anyone with the link.

findings.title: The webcam bubble stops all webcam tracks when it is destroyed, but the recorder's compositor owns and still uses that stream, so unmounting the bubble during or right after a recording kills the webcam feed.
findings.description: The webcam bubble stops all webcam tracks when it is destroyed, but the recorder's compositor owns and still uses that stream, so unmounting the bubble during or right after a recording kills the webcam feed.

findings.title: The path allowlist for reading recordings compares the canonicalized request against un-canonicalized directories, so on macOS, where the temp directory sits under the /var symlink, every file in the app's own temp recording directory is refused and the preview cannot load a fresh recording.
findings.description: The path allowlist for reading recordings compares the canonicalized request against un-canonicalized directories, so on macOS, where the temp directory sits under the /var symlink, every file in the app's own temp recording directory is refused and the preview cannot load a fresh recording.

findings.title: get_config and save_config are plain synchronous Tauri commands that do blocking keychain and file I/O, so they run on the main thread and freeze the window while the keychain answers.
findings.description: get_config and save_config are plain synchronous Tauri commands that do blocking keychain and file I/O, so they run on the main thread and freeze the window while the keychain answers.

findings.title: The allowlist for reading files accepts any path under the system temp directory, so the webview can read any other app's temp files, not just this app's recordings.
